query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: If stainless steel is subjected to low-temperature plasma nitriding at about 400–500 °C in a controlled nitrogen atmosphere, the nitrogen-enriched surface (expanded austenite) will form and significantly increase corrosion resistance without severely compromising core properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Austenitic stainless steel in the annealed condition.
generation.intervention: Apply low-temperature plasma nitriding in a controlled nitrogen atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Moderate nitriding temperatures (~400–500 °C) maintained for typical exposure times, with controlled nitrogen partial pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of nitrogen-enriched expanded austenite in the near-surface region.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen incorporation enhances passivation and reduces corrosion susceptibility on the treated surface.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved corrosion resistance compared to untreated stainless steel, while retaining bulk mechanical properties.
generation.baseline: Untreated stainless steel exposed to the same corrosive environment under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness may diminish at higher temperatures or if process parameters (time, pressure, temperature) deviate significantly from the suggested conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal plasma nitriding parameters (exact temperature, time, and gas composition) for each specific stainless steel composition are not fully determined in the provided context.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of austenitic stainless steel coupons. Treat one set with low-temperature plasma nitriding in a controlled nitrogen atmosphere at ~450 °C. Expose both treated and untreated samples to a corrosive environment (e.g., salt spray or acidic solution) under identical conditions for a defined period.
measurements: Mass loss per unit area to quantify corrosion rate
Surface composition via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided coupons do not exhibit a measurable improvement in corrosion resistance compared to untreated controls, the hypothesis is falsified.
